text: Sleep is the world's most powerful PED. Your body is 80% what you eat and 20% everything else. The most important variable in your training is intensity. You need to track your lifts over time if you ever want to gain muscle. There's no such thing as getting toned. Low weights for high reps does nothing but exhaust you. Stick to the five to 15 rep range. Two workouts per week is all you need to make excellent progress. The most important diet rule is 80% single-ingredient foods. Training your legs boosts your testosterone, which helps everything else grow. Soreness does not equate to progress. Calisthenics builds proportion, weights build size. You don't need to do three sets. One to two to failure is more than enough. Keep alcohol to one day per week. Lifting heavy by itself does not make you bulky. To get big, you must eat big. The best lower body exercise is Bulgarian split squats. You can get jacked with nothing but calisthenics and a good diet. If you struggle to grow a particular body part, move it to the start of your workout. If you don't want money problems, you must count your money. The same applies to your calories. Planning your meals in advance gives you the best chance to succeed. You don't need to be perfect, but you must be consistent. Your meals should revolve around 30 grams of protein. Most supplements are bullshit, and if you like to weigh yourself, you should do so every morning on an empty stomach and only pay attention to the weekly average.
